To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel immunosuppressive mAb was identified from MS patients with a stable disease course.
a mAb to CD64 was isolated from long-term stable RR-MS patients and that it exerts immunosuppressive properties on MS-derived T cells and on monocytes.

(1) a mAb to the CD64 receptor, isolated from EBV(+)-B cell clones of MS patients with long-term remission, exerts immunosuppressive properties on MS T cells, and (2) the biological basis of this immunosuppression is the induction and release of IL-10 and decreased IL-12 levels from activated monocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel mAb to CD64 that may have therapeutic potential in MS.
the development and testing of novel immunosuppressive agents in the context of MS.

the identification and characterization of novel immunosuppressive antibodies from patients with long term stable RRMS, which might be useful in the treatment of immune-mediated neurological disorders, including MS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mAb to CD64 is a novel therapeutic approach to MS and other immune mediated neurological disorders.
the anti-CD64 monoclonal antibody has been isolated from EBV-positive B cell clones of MS patients.
the mAb 3D6 has a high therapeutic potential for MS patients and should be considered as a new treatment option for patients with MS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunosuppressive CD64 mAb is an important new immunotherapeutic tool for MS and other autoimmune diseases.
we have isolated a new mAb that may be used as a new therapeutic tool to modulate the immune response in MS and other immune-related disorders.
we have identified a new mAb to the Fc receptor of the B cell, CD64.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a mAb to the extracellular domain 222-228 of the high affinity immunoglobulins gamma Fc-receptors (FcγRI) is capable of exerting immunomodulatory activity on activated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) and on activated T cells from MS patients.
the immunosuppressive monocloal antibodies isolated from RRMS patients are capable to induce a tolerogenic phenotype in T and B cells and in monocytes.
we have identified a mAb to MBPs that has immunosuppressive properties in vitro, which may have a potential role in the treatment of autoimmune neurological diseases.
